title: Give your AI something to work with
bullets: Context that sticks. A link anyone can open.
Week 6 · Learn, Vibe, Build · October 5, 2026
notes: 5:05–5:06. Three simple demos: copy the lesson, context that sticks, getting online. No live connector tonight.

title: Demo 1 · copy the lesson
bullets: Copy the lesson markdown into your AI.
Ask: “Teach me this and quiz me.”
Check its explanation against the lesson.
notes: 5:06–5:11. Open cu.learnvibe.build/lessons/week-6/, click Copy lesson as markdown, paste into a fresh chat. Ask exactly: Teach me this and quiz me. Answer one question. If it stalls, use the real rehearsal output on the demo script page.

title: Markdown is just a text file
bullets: A .md file is plain text, with headings and lists.
You can read it. Your AI can read it.
Context can live in a file instead of your memory.
notes: 5:11–5:12. Show the raw lesson. Point to # headings and - bullets; no syntax lesson beyond that.

title: Context that sticks
bullets: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md at session start.
Cursor and other coding tools can load AGENTS.md.
In a chat app: paste the file or add it to a Project.
notes: 5:12–5:13. These are ordinary markdown files in your project. Specific support varies by tool; Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, and our tested installation also found AGENTS.md. No template or prescribed structure. Say what you would tell a new teammate.

title: One small example
bullets: # Hill Plant Swap
A one-page website for a free monthly plant swap on the Hill, near CU.
It's for first-year students who are nervous about going.
Keep it plain HTML and CSS. No JavaScript.
Only use the facts in docs/event-facts.md. Never make up dates or places.
notes: 5:13–5:15. Write these five lines live as CLAUDE.md. This is one example, not a template. The extra facts help the agent aim at the actual audience.

title: Demo 2 · ask again
bullets: Ask about the small project, cold.
Add the short context file. Ask again.
Start a fresh session: does it still know?
notes: 5:15–5:23. Use Hill Plant Swap. Exact prompt: Improve the homepage. Don’t edit any files: describe the changes you’d make in 6 bullets or fewer. Compare audience, unnecessary RSVP, simplicity. Start a third fresh session: Without reading any files, what is this project, and what should you never do? If delayed, use real captured results on demo script.

title: A link someone else can open
bullets: file:///Users/you/Desktop/index.html
Only on your laptop.
https://you.github.io/project/
A published website.
notes: 5:23–5:24. Local files and localhost links aren’t public. Open the published link on another phone.

title: Save. Send. Publish.
bullets: Commit: a save point on your laptop.
Push: send it to GitHub.
Deploy: turn it into a live website.
notes: 5:24–5:25. Explain these as three different steps.

title: Demo 3 · getting online
bullets: GitHub Desktop: create, commit, publish.
GitHub → Settings → Pages → main → Save.
Open the live link on a phone.
notes: 5:25–5:31. Use plain-folder zip. Commit first version, publish public repo, Settings Pages main root. If waiting, show pre-deployed Hill Plant Swap. React/Vite/Next app: Vercel instead. Handout covers exact clicks.

title: Next week: your AI reaches your tools
bullets: API: one program asking another for something.
Connector: your AI reaches your tools directly.
Instead of you pasting. Next week we’ll connect.
notes: 5:31–5:33. Concept only. A connector often uses a standard called Model Context Protocol. Don’t show a server URL or set one up. This week, copying the markdown is the step toward that.

title: This week’s reading: your AI as a coach
bullets: Arielle Shipper · How to Get Better at AI by Asking AI
Give your AI examples of how you’ve worked.
Ask it to teach you one next step.
notes: 5:33–5:35. Free link on account page. No history? Paste last two submissions. No due date. Then trios 5:35–6:05.

title: Studio: build
bullets: Work on your project.
Optional: ask your AI what it needs to know.
Save that context as a markdown file.
notes: 6:05–7:05. No prescribed pairs or interview exercise. Build, test, help each other as needed. 7:05–7:35 optional studio.
